name: RI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+12) in a seat Democrats hold comfortably
Overwhelming cash advantage: Amo has $1.85M on hand vs. about $2,300 for Keenan
Prediction markets price the Democratic win probability near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; Republican challenger is low-profile and barely funded
model.rationale: The district's twelve-point Democratic lean, Amo's incumbency and his roughly 750-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent Democratic leave no evident path for the underfunded Republican challenger. The forecast holds at a safe Democratic win with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any polling showing a single-digit race or a late wave of outside spending against Amo would be the main trigger for revision.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rhode Island's first district leans about twelve points Democratic, and incumbent Gabe Amo enters the general election with an overwhelming financial edge. He has raised about $1.7 million and holds roughly $1.85 million on hand, while Republican Kellie Keenan has raised little more than $12,000 and reports about $2,300 in the bank. An independent candidate, Pedro DeSouza, is also on the ballot but reports no fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97 percent. With the seat's strong Democratic lean, Amo's incumbency, and his resource advantage, the main question in this race is the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
